answer.answer: The mean concentration in the last third of sampled years (2010-2012) was 10.34 times higher than in the first third (2001-2003), but this does not clearly show a rise in Pacific plastic because the sampling locations shifted substantially (centroid shift of ~1042 km) across years, and the weak Spearman correlation (rho=0.168) suggests the trend may largely reflect spatial sampling differences rather than a true temporal increase.
